text.p: Stocks soared Wednesday on expectations of continued economic growth after President Clinton won re-election and Republicans retained control of Congress.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 62.62 points at 6,143.80, handily surpassing its record closing high of 6,094.23 set on Oct. 18.
The New York Stock Exchange's curbs on index-arbitrage trading were activated when the Dow gained 50 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines 2-1 on active volume of 286 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 10.64 points at 1,239.71. The American Stock Exchange index was up 3.40 at 577.02.
Bonds were steady, with the yield on the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond inching up to 6.60 from Tuesday's close of 6.59 percent after initially dropping to 6.57 percent -- the lowest since March 7.

Democrat Clinton easily turned back Republican challenger Bob Dole on Tuesday, but the GOP held its small majorities in both houses of Congress, setting the stage for continuing moderation in fiscal policy.
"This is probably the least inflationary course that could have been taken, so there's lots of optimism," said Edgar Peters, chief investment strategist at Boston-based PanAgora Asset Management Inc.
"Everyone's happy. The Street is very comfortable with the idea of a Republican Congress keeping spending down," he said.
Analysts said they believed the division of power in Washington was the best course.
Wall Street had worried that if Democrats won control of two branches of the federal government they might have increased spending.

Analysts also said the split was preferable to Bob Dole winning the presidency, since many Wall Street economists thought the Republicans would have failed to find spending cuts to match their proposed tax cuts.
Technology stocks were big gainers as a buying spree in the sector followed the defeat of a controversial proposition in California that would have allowed shareholders to sue companies more easily.
Among technology stocks, Intel Corp. rose 2 to 116, Hewlett-Packard gained 1 to 45-1/8, and Advanced Micro Devices gained 3/8 to 19-1/2.
Intuit Inc. was up 6 at 35-1/2 on rumours that American Expresss was planning to launch a bid for the personal finance software company.

Tobacco, drug, biotechnology and health maintenance organisation stocks surged, on speculation that a Republican Congress will keep the Clinton administration from aggressively regulating the industries, analysts said.
Drug stocks were up across the board, with Merck & Co. rising 1-5/8 to 77-3/8, Pfizer Inc. up 2-1/2 to 88-1/8 and Bristol-Myers Squibb advancing 3 to 111-1/2.
United Healthcare jumped 2-3/4 to 40 while Oxford Health Plans Inc., rose 3 to 49-7/8.
Among biotech stocks, Biogen Inc. gained 2 to 75-3/4 and Centocor Inc., climbed 1-1/2 to 27-7/8.
